institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The aspects that were crucial in choosing my study destination were the culture, the university and being able to experience beautiful nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My whole exchange experience could not be better. Trondheim is a fantastic city with a huge number of young people, which created a great youth environment. In addition, Norway is just a fantastic country if you also want to experience beautiful nature and go on some wild trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find all the knowledge and information I needed when I arrived in Trondheim, as NTNU is really good at receiving exchange students and sending all the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome week where NTNU had made sure that various things happened, such as getting the information you needed for the study and other more social things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I had a bit of trouble finding accommodation to start with. I think I started in good time by writing to people on a website called
hybel.no
, but not many people responded. When we got very close to departure, I ended up finding a dorm room and it was very easy, I think they only became available right before the start of the semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's super nice and there are many different options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would not recommend living in a dormitory as we were many exchange students who were put in the same kitchen, which meant that no one had respect for things or cleaned. So if I had to do it again myself, I would have tried to find an apartment with some roomies to live with (I can recommend Norwegian roomies - the other Danes were very happy about that)!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't quite remember the process itself, but I do remember that it was very easy and that NTNU generally takes care of many of the things that need to be done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went perfectly fine. You could sign up for all the courses you thought sounded interesting and then after a month there was a deadline to unregister the ones you didn't want anyway. So for a whole month you could change courses if you found out that there was a course you would rather have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to worry so much about that. It's easy and you get all the information you need from NTNU, even if you've forgotten something.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, the level was the same or lower than KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Condensed introduction to Neuroscience, Molecular Medical Bacteriology, Introduction to Social Psychology and Psychological Disorders

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in psychology, I would definitely recommend Psychological Disorders!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport was cheaper than I thought. Food was about the same. Alcohol was much more expensive than I thought. And otherwise it was like living in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Trondheim has a lot of offers regardless of what you are interested in.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are generally many student-run organizations that offer various things such as sports activities, musical activities etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend that you become a member of something called NTNUI and Samfundet. NTNUI is a sports organization where you can sign up for different sports and try new things. Samfundet is a social organization where there are many fun events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lapland and Lofoten!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the culture is the same as Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't really have any tips as I was mostly with other Danes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The same things as in Denmark - people are very sweet, open and helpfull.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You don't have to worry about the formal things - you get help with those. Choose some courses that don't take up too much of your time so you can spend it on other social things and experiences. Look forward to it - it's a fantastic city and NTNU is a really good university!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the sweet friends I've made!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on your own in a new country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
